title: 5d PRD: constraint system + DD integration
description:
# PRD: constraint system + DD integration

Phase 5d capability PRD. Builds the constraint system (Layer 3) on top of
sutra's differential dataflow engine, providing human-authored architectural
rules that are incrementally checked as the codebase evolves.

Brainstorm decisions: sutra/42. Architecture context: `sutra-architecture.md`,
`sutra-vision.md` (L3 section). Core model foundation: `prd-core-model.md`.
DD spike: `docs/v1-spikes/differential-dataflow.md` (on `spike/hdc-ast-encoding`).

## Problem statement

Sutra can detect conventions (what the code does) and flag deviations, but it
cannot enforce constraints (what the code must do). An architect who decides
"the database layer must never import HTTP types" has no way to express that
as a live, incrementally checked rule. The existing `rules.toml` supports only
flat forbidden-dep pairs with no severity, no provenance, no component-level
boundaries, and no waiver mechanism. The DD engine maintains cycle and blast
radius views but checks forbidden deps ad-hoc at query time, losing the
automatic incrementality that is DD's core value.

Without a constraint system, architectural invariants exist only in the
architect's head or in prose ADRs — neither of which sutra can check.

## Solution

Introduce a constraint system that lets architects declare rules in
`.sutra/rules.toml`, checks them incrementally via DD maintained views, and
integrates into orient (so agents know what's required), review (so the
architect sees violations), and guard (so violations block when configured).

Constraints are human-authored (provenance: human-authored or ADR-derived),
carry per-instance severity, and support waivers. Component-level boundary
constraints are resolved to file-level forbidden pairs via the component
membership table, keeping DD simple (file IDs only).

## User stories

1. As an architect, I want to declare that component "db" must not import
   component "http," so that the boundary is enforced incrementally without
   manual review.

2. As an architect, I want each constraint to carry a severity (blocking,
   advisory, informational), so that I control which violations prevent merge
   and which are flagged for judgment.

3. As an architect, I want to reference an ADR in a constraint's provenance
   field, so that anyone reading a violation can trace it to the design
   decision that motivates it.

4. As an architect, I want to declare that a subgraph must be acyclic, so
   that cycle detection targets the areas I care about rather than the entire
   codebase.

5. As an architect, I want to set a max-fan-in threshold on a file or symbol,
   so that coupling hotspots are flagged before they become unmanageable.

6. As an architect, I want constraint violations to update within 100ms of
   saving a file, so that I get near-real-time feedback during development.

7. As an architect, I want to waive a specific constraint violation with a
   rationale, so that intentional exceptions are tracked rather than silently
   ignored.

8. As an architect, I want waived violations to appear in every review report
   that touches the waived area, so that I can audit accepted exceptions over
   time.

9. As an agent receiving orient output, I want to see the constraints that
   apply to the area I'm about to edit, so that I write code that respects
   architectural rules, not just conventions.

10. As an agent receiving orient output, I want to see active waivers in the
    area, so that I know where intentional exceptions exist and don't
    "fix" them.

11. As a reviewer running `sutra review`, I want to see which constraint
    violations were introduced by the current change and which were resolved,
    so that the review shows the delta, not just the current state.

12. As a reviewer, I want constraint violations to carry enough context
    (constraint kind, severity, provenance, component) that I can assess them
    without looking up the rule definition separately.

13. As the guard hook, I want to block commits that introduce blocking
    constraint violations, so that architectural rules are enforced at the
    git boundary.

14. As the guard hook, I want advisory and informational violations to be
    reported but not block the commit, so that enforcement is proportional.

15. As an architect writing an ADR with an agent, I want to write a
    constraint for the ADR in the same session, so that the decision is
    immediately self-enforcing.

16. As an architect, I want the old `[constraints]` format to keep working
    during transition, so that existing rules.toml files don't break when I
    upgrade.

17. As an architect, I want to name a constraint (optional), so that I can
    reference it in waivers and conversation by a human-readable label
    instead of a hash.

18. As a sutra contributor, I want constraint violations in the review
    pipeline to follow the same waiver-partition pattern as convention
    violations, so that the two systems stay structurally parallel.

19. As a sutra contributor, I want the DD module renamed from `dd/` to
    `constraints/` before new work lands, so that the module name reflects
    its concern.

20. As a sutra contributor, I want the constraint resolver (component
    boundaries to file-level pairs) to be a separate, testable module, so
    that boundary resolution logic is not entangled with DD internals.

21. As a sutra contributor, I want the DD worker to accept a second input
    collection for forbidden pairs, so that forbidden-dep checking becomes a
    maintained view rather than an ad-hoc query-time intersection.

22. As the convention system (5c), I want no data dependency on the
    constraint system, so that the two tracks remain independently
    evolvable.

## Implementation decisions

### Module rename: dd/ → constraints/

First PR. Mechanical refactor — `src/dd/` becomes `src/constraints/`, all
`use crate::dd::` imports update, `mod dd` in `lib.rs` becomes
`mod constraints`. Same internal structure (engine, worker, mod), new name.
Aligns with architecture doc's naming-by-concern convention.

### Constraint authoring format

Hybrid: well-typed TOML patterns for common constraint kinds. Future
Datalog-like escape hatch is out of scope.

Each constraint is a TOML table in a `[[constraint]]` array in
`.sutra/rules.toml`. Fields:

- `kind` — required. One of: `forbidden_dep`, `boundary`, `max_fan_in`,
  `no_cycles`.
- `severity` — optional, defaults per kind. One of: `blocking` (default for
  forbidden_dep, boundary, no_cycles), `advisory` (default for max_fan_in),
  `informational`.
- `name` — optional human-readable label. Used in waiver references and
  orient output.
- `provenance` — optional. Path to ADR or free-text rationale.
- `scope` — optional. Path prefix or component name restricting where the
  constraint applies.
- Kind-specific fields: `from`/`to` for forbidden_dep,
  `from_component`/`to_component` for boundary, `target`/`threshold` for
  max_fan_in, no additional fields for no_cycles (uses scope).

### Constraint identity

Blake3 hash of `(kind, normalized_params)`. Deterministic, stable across
re-reads of the same rules file. The optional `name` field is an alias —
waivers can reference by hash prefix or name. Matches how conventions use
hash-based identity, with human naming added since constraints are authored.

### Backward compatibility

The old `[constraints]` section with `forbidden_deps = [...]` continues to
parse. Internally converted to `Constraint` structs with kind
`forbidden_dep`, severity `blocking`, no provenance. Both formats readable;
the new `[[constraint]]` format is canonical.

### Boundary enforcement via resolver

DD operates on file IDs only — it knows nothing about components. A new
resolver module resolves component-level boundary constraints to file-level
forbidden pairs by joining `boundary` constraints against the
`component_membership` table.

Resolution triggers: component membership changes (recompute) or constraint
file changes. Resolved pairs are cached with a generation counter on
component_membership; re-resolved when generation bumps.

Resolved forbidden pairs feed into DD as a second input collection, making
boundary enforcement a maintained view — violations update automatically on
both edge changes and membership changes.

### DD engine evolution

The worker gains a second input collection for forbidden pairs. The existing
single-input (import edges) design extends to:

1. **Import edges** — from Layer 0 parse deltas (unchanged).
2. **Forbidden pairs** — from constraint resolution. A maintained view
   computes `edges ∩ forbidden_pairs → violations`.

Forbidden-dep checking moves from ad-hoc query-time intersection
(`query_forbidden_deps` with rules passed in) to a maintained DD view that
updates automatically. The `Command` enum gains a `SetForbiddenPairs` variant.

Cycle detection and blast radius views remain unchanged.

### Richer violation output

`ConstraintViolation` gains: `constraint_id` (hash), `constraint_name`
(optional), `constraint_kind`, `severity`, `provenance`,
`component_context`. Violations carry enough context for review reports and
orient output without re-joining against the constraint store.

### Constraint waivers (durable table)

Same pattern as `convention_waivers`. New `constraint_waivers` durable table:
`constraint_id` (TEXT), `file_path` or `symbol_qualified_name` (scope of
waiver), `rationale` (required, TEXT), `created_at`, `updated_at`. Waivers
reference constraints by hash or name. Waived violations appear in review
reports with their waiver rationale.

### Constraint diffing in review

The review tool reports the delta: violations introduced by the change vs
violations resolved. Implementation: compare violations involving changed
files before and after the diff's edges are applied. DD's epoch mechanism
supports this — snapshot violations at the pre-change epoch, advance, compare.

### Orient integration

`sutra_orient` gains a constraints section: active constraints scoped to the
target area, any active waivers, and any current violations. Follows the same
scope-resolution logic as convention orientation.

### MCP tool surface

New actions on the constraints tool (or extension of existing tools):
- `list` — all constraints with their resolution status
- `violations` — current constraint violations
- `waive` — create a waiver with rationale
- `unwaive` — revoke a waiver

### Trust model integration

Severity is per-constraint-instance, set by the author. Defaults:
`forbidden_dep` → blocking, `boundary` → blocking, `no_cycles` → blocking,
`max_fan_in` → advisory. Guard blocks on blocking violations only; advisory
and informational are reported.

Sketch mode (ADR-0001): constraints remain fully enforced in sketch-mode
components. This is unchanged — constraints are prescriptive and binding
regardless of prototyping state.

### Independence from 5c (conventions)

No data dependency. Constraints operate on Layer 0 structural edges;
conventions operate on Layer 0 + FCA attributes. Shared infrastructure:
DB, review pipeline, orient, guard. Separate tables, separate types, separate
engines. The review pipeline is a thin aggregator that calls both.

## Testing decisions

Tests verify external behavior through module interfaces, not implementation
details. Prior art: `tests/dd-test.rs` (DD engine), `tests/db-test.rs`
(DB operations), `tests/review-test.rs` (integration).

### Modules to test

**Constraints module (`src/constraints/`):**
- Engine lifecycle: cold → warm → loaded transitions, eviction.
- Cycle detection: ingest edges with a cycle, query returns correct SCCs.
  Add/remove edge that creates/breaks a cycle, verify incremental update.
- Blast radius: ingest edges, query returns correct reachability counts.
  Incremental update on edge change.
- Forbidden pairs maintained view: set forbidden pairs, ingest edges that
  include a forbidden pair, verify violation appears. Remove the edge, verify
  violation disappears. Change forbidden pairs, verify violations update.
- Boundary resolution: mock component membership + boundary constraints,
  verify resolver produces correct file-level forbidden pairs. Change
  membership, verify re-resolution. Cache hit when membership unchanged.
- Behavioral parity: existing `dd-test.rs` tests must pass against renamed
  module with no behavior change.

**Rules module (`src/rules.rs`):**
- New format parsing: `[[constraint]]` with all fields (kind, severity, name,
  provenance, scope, kind-specific fields). Verify round-trip identity hash.
- Old format parsing: `[constraints]` with `forbidden_deps` still works,
  produces correct `Constraint` structs with default severity.
- Mixed format: both old and new sections in one file, no conflict.
- Edge cases: missing optional fields get correct defaults. Unknown kind
  produces a clear error. Duplicate constraint (same hash) is deduplicated.
- Constraint identity: same params → same hash. Different params → different
  hash. Name does not affect hash.

**DB module (`src/db/constraints.rs`):**
- Waiver CRUD: create waiver with rationale, read it back, update rationale,
  delete. Waiver survives reindex (durable table).
- Waiver scoping: waiver for specific file_path, waiver for
  symbol_qualified_name. Query waivers applicable to a given file/symbol.
- Orphan detection: create waiver for constraint X, change rules so X no
  longer exists, detect orphan.
- Migration: new tables created correctly, partition metadata correct.

Test setup: `Db::open_unchecked("test", dir.path())` with tempdir, consistent
with existing test patterns.

## Out of scope

- **Datalog-like custom constraint DSL.** The hybrid approach covers common
  patterns; a richer language is a future layer.
- **Auto-parsing ADRs to extract constraints.** The workflow is human+agent
  writes constraint alongside ADR; no NLP extraction.
- **Component discovery (5b).** This PRD consumes components; it does not
  create or manage them.
- **Convention system changes.** 5c is independent. No modifications to FCA
  engine, convention lifecycle, drift detection, or templates.
- **PageRank in DD.** Spike confirmed non-monotone iteration is a bad fit.
  Stays imperative.
- **Co-change in DD.** Git-based, no incremental benefit.
- **Real-time component-level aggregations.** Coupling metrics between
  components via DD deferred — component membership changes infrequently.
- **Constraint UI/visualization.** Constraints are managed via MCP tools and
  TOML files. A visual dashboard is separate work.
- **Per-directory constraint files.** Constraints are workspace-level. Scope
  is handled by the `scope` field on the constraint, not file placement.

## Further notes

### Evolution ordering

The PRs should land in order:

1. **Module rename** (`dd/` → `constraints/`) — pure rename, no behavior
   change. Unblocks everything.
2. **Constraint types + rules parsing** — new `Constraint` struct,
   `[[constraint]]` format, identity hashing, backward compat. No DD
   changes yet.
3. **DD forbidden pairs view** — second input collection, maintained
   violation view. Replaces ad-hoc `query_forbidden_deps`.
4. **Boundary resolver** — component membership → file-level forbidden
   pairs. Plugs into the DD forbidden pairs input.
5. **DB: constraint waivers** — durable waiver table, CRUD methods, waiver
   partition in review.
6. **Review + orient integration** — richer violation output, constraint
   diffing, orient constraint section, guard severity filtering.
7. **MCP tools** — constraint list, violations, waive/unwaive actions.

### Risk areas

- **DD second input collection** is the most technically novel change. The
  spike demonstrated forbidden deps as a maintained view, but the current
  engine has a single-input architecture. Extending the timely dataflow to
  two inputs requires care with the probe/timestamp model.
- **Boundary resolver correctness** depends on component_membership being
  accurate. If clustering produces unstable membership, boundary violations
  will flicker. The generation-counter cache helps (don't re-resolve on
  every query), but the root stability comes from Layer 1 component design.
- **Backward compatibility** in rules parsing. The old format must keep
  working for existing users. Test both paths explicitly.
